title: SQL injection in product search endpoint
description: The /products/search endpoint builds its SQL query by concatenating the user-supplied q parameter directly into the string at line 41. No parameterization is used, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary SQL including UNION-based attacks.
evidence: GET /products/search?q=%27%20OR%201%3D1%20-- returned all 6 products instead of zero results.

title: JWT signature verification disabled on /auth/refresh enables impersonation
description: The /auth/refresh endpoint decodes JWTs with verify_signature=False at line 101. Any crafted JWT payload is accepted regardless of signature validity. The endpoint trusts whatever sub claim appears in the forged token to look up and re-issue a real session for that user.
evidence: POST /auth/refresh with unsigned forged JWT containing sub=1 returned HTTP 200 with a freshly signed valid JWT for user 1. GET /account confirmed identity as user 1 (Priya Shah).

title: Stored XSS via review body rendered unescaped in product pages
description: Review bodies submitted via POST /products/id/reviews are stored after minimal validation but not sanitized. The Jinja2 template renders review bodies with the safe filter at product.html line 13, bypassing autoescaping. An attacker can inject script tags or javascript: URIs.
evidence: POST /products/1/reviews with body=<script>alert(1)</script> succeeded with 201. GET /p/MUG-SPECK returned HTML containing the raw script tag inside div.review-body.

title: Insecure Direct Object Reference - order details accessible to any authenticated user
description: The show_order function calls get_order which selects ANY order by ID without verifying the requesting user owns the order. Any authenticated user can view another user's order details including items, prices, payment amounts, refund history, and delivery dates.
evidence: Authenticated as user 1, GET /orders/1 returned complete details of Priya Shah's order. Even without Authorization header, the auth decorator bug allowed unauthenticated access returning full order data.

title: Auth decorator swallows HTTPException, allowing unauthenticated access to protected endpoints
description: The @require_auth decorator wraps authentication in a try/except Exception block. When abort(401) raises Flask HTTPException at line 54, it is caught by except Exception, g.user is set to None, and execution continues to the route handler. Endpoints not referencing g.user return data unauthenticated; those referencing g.user crash with 500 errors.
evidence: GET /orders/1 with no Authorization header returned HTTP 200 with full order data. GET /orders with no auth returned 500 Internal Server Error due to AttributeError when accessing g.user id.

title: SQL injection in admin review lookup via unsanitized display_name
description: The /admin/reports/reviews endpoint constructs its SQL query using Python f-string interpolation with customer display_name at line 80. While this requires staff authentication, the display_name value was originally user-controlled input (settable via PATCH /account) and stored without sanitization.
evidence: Set user 1 display_name to SQL injection payload via PATCH /account. GET /admin/reports/reviews?customer_id=1 as staff triggered HTTP 500 Internal Server Error.

title: Payment confirmation marks order as paid when provider times out
description: When the external payment provider does not respond within the timeout period, the confirm_payment handler sets status=paid at line 42 and unconditionally updates the order to processing with paid_pence equal to total_pence. If the payment actually failed but only the network timed out, the customer receives goods without paying.
evidence: Code at payments.py lines 37-45: except requests.Timeout branch sets status=paid then falls through to if status==paid update to processing with full amount credited.

title: Passwords hashed with unsalted single-pass SHA-256
description: Password hashing at line 16 uses hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest() with no salt, pepper, or iterative stretching. This enables offline brute-force and rainbow table attacks across all users simultaneously.
evidence: def hash_password(password): return hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest() - single-pass SHA-256, no salt, no work factor.

title: Password reset token has only ~27 bits of entropy from non-cryptographic RNG
description: The reset token at line 135 is generated with 8-digit decimal number producing max 100 million possibilities using the random module which is deterministic and not cryptographically secure. Combined with a 30-minute validity window, brute-force recovery is feasible.
evidence: token = %08d % int(random.random() * 10**8) produces only 8 digits (~27 bits entropy). With 30-minute expiry, exhaustive search is feasible over network.

title: Secret key hardcoded in source code
description: SECRET_KEY is a static string committed to the repository. Since JWT tokens use HS256 with this key, anyone reading the source code can forge valid JWT tokens for any user with any role.
evidence: SECRET_KEY = hf-shop-2f8a1c9e7b4d visible in plain text in config.py line 3.

title: Flask debug mode enabled in production deployment
description: debug=True is passed to app.run() at line 6, enabling Werkzeug interactive debugger and auto-reloader. If an exception occurs, the debugger presents an interactive Python console that could allow remote code execution if the PIN is guessable.

title: Unrestricted CORS with credentials allowed from any origin
description: The CORS middleware at lines 44-50 echoes back the requester Origin header unconditionally as Access-Control-Allow-Origin and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials true. Any website can make authenticated cross-origin requests.
evidence: GET /products with Origin https://evil.example.com returned headers Access-Control-Allow-Origin https://evil.example.com and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials true.

title: Sensitive request bodies including plaintext passwords logged to server logs
description: At line 31, all POST/PUT/PATCH request bodies are logged in full (truncated to 2000 characters) via log.info(). Registration requests contain plaintext passwords, exposing credentials in log output accessible to operators or monitoring systems.
evidence: log.info with request.get_data(as_text=True)[:2000] captures entire request body including passwords sent during registration.

title: Unsafe pickle deserialization of browser-controlled cookie data
description: The basket cookie at line 20 is deserialized with pickle.loads from data controlled by the browser. Pickle supports arbitrary object instantiation, meaning a crafted cookie payload can trigger remote code execution. No integrity check validates the cookie before loading.
evidence: pickle.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(raw)) at line 20 reads raw data from browser-controlled basket cookie without HMAC or signature verification.

title: User enumeration via distinct login error messages
description: The login endpoint returns different error messages for non-existent emails versus wrong password for existing accounts, allowing attackers to enumerate valid email addresses.
evidence: POST /auth/login with nonexistent@nobody.com returned error no account with that email. POST with priya.shah@mail.test + bad password returned wrong password.
